hook.say: The morning post said an architect tested 13 models, and Opus 5.5 produced a drawing set he judges permit-quality. I went back in to check the numbers around it.

findings.label: COST
findings.headline: Codersera lists Opus 5.5 at $5.98 per index task
findings.detail: We could not find this cost on the cited page at check time.
findings.evidence: Opus 5.5 costs $5.98 per completed index task against Opus 5's $5.86
findings.say: First, Codersera lists $5.98 per completed task for Opus 5.5 against $5.86 for Opus 5, but we could not confirm it on their page.

findings.label: VS GPT-6
findings.headline: Opus 5.5 cost per task vs GPT-6 Sol
findings.detail: Token prices are $4/$20 for Opus 5.5 and $2/$10 for GPT-6 Sol, per million tokens.
findings.evidence: the cost per evaluation task is roughly 5.4 times higher than Sol's.
findings.say: Second, MindStudio's comparison puts Opus 5.5 at 5.4 times GPT-6 Sol's cost per evaluation task, with token prices double.

findings.label: RANKING
findings.headline: BenchLM score out of 100, ranked #2 of 216 models
findings.detail: A general benchmark score, not a drafting test.
findings.evidence: Claude Opus 5.5 scores 86.3 out of 100 and ranks #2 of 216.
findings.say: Third, BenchLM scores Opus 5.5 at 86.3 out of 100, second of 216 models. Strong, but a general score, not drafting.

take.headline: Cheaper tokens are not a cheaper result.
take.say: Cheaper tokens may not mean a cheaper result. If you use Opus 5.5, what do you pay per finished task? Comment CHECK and tell me.

sources.title: Codersera - Claude Opus 5.5: Specs, Pricing & Benchmarks
MindStudio - GPT-6 Sol vs Claude Opus 5.5 pricing
BenchLM - Claude Opus 5.5 Benchmarks, Pricing & Speed

caption:
This morning: an architect tested 13 AI models, and Claude Opus 5.5 produced a drawing set he judges good enough for a building permit.

The deep dive: Codersera lists $5.98 per completed task for Opus 5.5, vs $5.86 for Opus 5. NOT CONFIRMED: we could not find this figure on the cited page. Also listed: 5.4x GPT-6 Sol's cost per evaluation task, and 86.3 out of 100 on BenchLM, ranked #2 of 216.

My take: cheaper tokens are not a cheaper result. Measure cost per finished, checked task.

Comment CHECK and I will DM you what I find.

Sources in the first comment.
